title: weekly-sync-serving-runtime-infra-console-agenda-prep-2026-02-25-evan
body:
Weekly Serving Runtime / Infra / Console Sync - prep notes (working doc)

Date/time: Tue 2026-03-03 10:00-11:00 PST (confirm) — trying to keep at 10am weekly.
Location: Zoom + #serving-runtime Slack thread
Attendees (anticipated): Evan, Maya, Diego, Jasmine, Arun (infra), Priya (console PD), optional: SRE on call (TBD)
Goal: Align on infra incidents, rollout status for runtime 2.1, console telemetry gaps, and clear action items for this week. Keep to 45 minutes for updates + 15 for blockers.

Tentative agenda (timeboxed):
- 10:00 - 10:05: Quick sync & roll call (Evan) — surface any new urgent items
- 10:05 - 10:20: Incident review / SLO anomalies (Arun + Diego) — 15m
   - current node GPU oom spikes last 48h (SR-1428)
   - autoscaler edge case: 2-min scale latency causing 50% of short sequences to timeout
- 10:20 - 10:35: Runtime 2.1 rollout status (Maya) — 15m
   - canary metrics: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, kv-cache hit rate
   - PR status: github.com/org/repo/pull/456 (rollout gating checks still pending)
- 10:35 - 10:45: Console observability gaps (Priya / Jasmine) — 10m
   - missing per-model token cost breakdown for dedicated clusters (customer ask)
   - tracing: need example traces for multi-model routing path
- 10:45 - 11:00: Blockers & action items (Evan) — 15m
   - finalize owners, due dates, and follow-ups

Prep notes / things to surface in meeting: 
- Incident SR-1428 details (Diego): GPU OOMs triggered by a small fraction of requests using long-cached KV contexts. Looks correlated with model variant switch. Logs attached in JIRA.
- Autoscaler behavior: observed 2x scaling thrash when bursty traffic + small backoff. Hypothesis: controller uses average CPU across pods; need pod-level request rate metric.
- Runtime 2.1 canary: p50 looks good, but p95 regressed ~7% vs 2.0 on sequence length 1024. Might be kernel selection fallback. We should gate rollout on p95 < +3% or revert.
- Console: customers keep asking for cost per route/model; the cost calc is available in backend but not surfaced per-token in UI. Priya wants a short-term UI workaround (CSV export) and long-term RU to add per-route breakdown.

Open questions to bring up:
- Do we throttle the canary traffic split until we fix the p95 regression? (Maya/Diego)
- What telemetry do we need from infra to detect autoscaler thrash proactively? (Arun)
- Who will own the console CSV workaround and what is the ETA? (Priya)

Proposed quick wins before meeting:
- Evan: attach canary logs + a short perf diff to the PR (done)
- Diego: surface example OOM stack traces in SR-1428 and add sample request IDs (in progress)
- Priya: prototype CSV export w/ per-route token/cost fields in staging (not started)

Action items (working tracker) - please treat as living checklist, update Jira/PRs as you progress:
- AI-001 | Owner: Diego | Task: Root cause analysis for GPU OOMs (SR-1428) — capture exact request shapes + model variant timeline | Due: 2026-03-05 | Status: in_progress
- AI-002 | Owner: Maya | Task: Hold canary at 10% and run targeted perf tests for seq len 1024/2048; try kernel pessimize flag off | Due: 2026-03-04 | Status: in_progress
- AI-003 | Owner: Arun | Task: Add per-pod request_rate metric to infra metrics pipeline and dashboard tile; alert if 95th request_rate spikes > 3x baseline | Due: 2026-03-10 | Status: todo
- AI-004 | Owner: Priya | Task: Implement temporary CSV export in console staging showing per-route token counts & cost estimate; link to billing mapping | Due: 2026-03-09 | Status: todo
- AI-005 | Owner: Evan | Task: Draft customer-facing note (internal) explaining canary pause criteria + rollback plan | Due: 2026-03-06 | Status: todo

Notes / talking points I want to raise: 
- Emphasize safety-first on canary gating; we can afford slower rollout if p95 is hit by >5%. Keep product teams in loop.
- For autoscaler, short-term band-aid: increase scale window to 5m for short-lived bursts; long-term: rate-based scaler.
- Console CSV export could be shipped as beta to a small set of customers using feature flag.

Attachments / links to include in meeting chat:
- JIRA SR-1428: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SR-1428
- Canary PR: https://github.com/org/repo/pull/456
- Perf dashboards (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/runtime-canary

Post-meeting follow-ups (template):
- Evan will update the action-items in this doc and copy to JIRA and Slack channel.
- Owners should update the JIRA ticket with progress and close the AI when done.

Personal notes / scratchpad items (not for meeting unless asked):
- Reminder: follow up with SRE to get runbook updated for OOMs (add sequence length/table of common culprit prompts).
- Keep a small set of synthetic prompts for reproducing kernel fallback — might help upstream kernel team.

Rough timeline this week:
- Thu 2026-03-05: target for Diego root cause findings
- Fri 2026-03-06: Evan draft of customer note
- Mon 2026-03-09: Priya CSV prototype demo in staging

If anyone wants to add an item, drop it below or ping me in Slack. I’ll finalize and send the calendar update 24h before the meeting.
summary: Working agenda + action item tracker for weekly sync between serving runtime, infra, and console teams. Drafted by Evan Chen. Focus: SR-1428 OOMs, runtime 2.1 canary p95 regression, console per-route cost visibility.
